page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-1xL40S is a GPU-accelerated virtual server deployed on KVM virtualization. The configuration couples 16 x86_64 vCPUs derived from an AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Architectural support includes extended vector instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, along with SHA-NI and AES cryptographic instructions. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU built on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, while local storage is not bundled.

Benchmark results highlight strong computational and accelerator metrics. Single-core throughput places in the top decile, demonstrated by a stress-ng score of 4172.89 and a Geekbench single-core result of 2825.0. Multi-threaded performance sits in the top quartile, with a stress-ng multi-core result of 67220.77 and a PassMark CPU score of 52859.8. Memory subsystem benchmarks show high throughput, sustaining 329.44 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 143.42 GB/sec for writes. In language model inference testing, the NVIDIA L40S executes small 135M model prompt processing at 3898.64 tokens/sec and text generation at 386.1 tokens/sec (both top 10%). Medium 7B model generation operates at 36.41 tokens/sec, while large 70B parameter inference decreases to 3.88 tokens/sec for generation and 12.03 tokens/sec for prompt processing.

The instance delivers a balanced ratio of 12 GB RAM per CPU core and a high-tier single-GPU accelerator, positioning it favorably for resource-intensive compute tasks without requiring multi-GPU node deployments. A primary engineering tradeoff is the absence of bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistent data, and the shared CPU core allocation model. The profile fits AI model inference, medium-scale machine learning fine-tuning, image and text processing pipelines, data transformation workloads, and in-memory caching systems such as Redis, which reached 67.91 million operations per second in testing.
